Classical two-square criterion and reciprocal-prime divergence in the class 3 mod 4
correctness.rationale: For the repaired positive-shift claim, −b/a is nonzero in F_q. The norm from the quadratic extension sends z to z^{q+1}, has kernel of size q+1 and is onto F_q^×. Its q+1 solutions modulo q are nonsingular because q is odd and neither a nor both coordinates vanish modulo q. Linear expansion modulo q² leaves exactly q lifts divisible by q² out of q² lifts per solution, giving (q+1)(q²−q)=q(q²−1) valuation-one pairs out of q⁴. These outputs are positive and are excluded by the two-square criterion. CRT gives the exact finite-set residue survivor fraction; box equidistribution is used only for fixed modulus. Since q⁻¹−q⁻³≥(8/9)q⁻¹ and the reciprocal sum of inert primes diverges after removing divisors of ab, the finite products make the nonnegative limsup zero. The frozen classification and zero-intercept arithmetic are correct, but the classification is prior coverage, not a new finding. The replacement does not include it as a contribution.
residual_risks: The tests recorded in the source are finite. The product measures survival of selected local tests, not representability; the theorem gives no rate and does not assert uniformity as a,b vary with H.

originality.rationale: This is a pass for the repaired claim only. The frozen record's standalone affine-preserver classification fails originality: Matijasevick Proposition 7.10(c) gives exactly that classification, including the same valuation-one witness argument. The repair removes the classification and homogeneous case from the finding and credits the source. The surviving positive-shift lattice-box zero-density theorem, exact residue count and finite-set product were not identified in the inspected earlier results. The local mechanism itself is standard and is not claimed as new.
residual_risks: A more general norm-value distribution or integral-parameter sieve theorem could cover the remaining density result; the comparison is bounded. No priority is asserted for the established affine-preserver classification or the standard lifting ingredients.

checked_sources: Matijasevick Proposition 7.10(c) for the contrast between failure of universal preservation and prevalence of success
value.rationale: An obstruction to preserving every input does not determine how often an affine shift succeeds on representations of an input norm. The repaired theorem proves that successful lattice pairs are negligible for every positive shift and fixed positive slope, and gives the exact loss per admissible prime and for any finite batch of tests. This provides a natural structural density statement with a directly reusable local factor, rather than repackaging the known classification or claiming only one explicit witness.
residual_risks: This is a qualitative limit, not an asymptotic count of the exceptional pairs or a claim about primitive norms or distinct integers.
